newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine c.bank clamps down on currency speculation.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine c.bank clamps down on currency speculation.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank will place tighter controls on buying and selling of foreign currencies by commercial banks to lessen speculative activity, the bank's chief said on Monday.
National Bank of Ukraine Chairman Viktor Yushchenko, addressing a news conference as the new hryvnia currency weakened, said:
"Based on the bank's reviews of activities, we can say that commercial banks do not always correctly apply the rules on the hard currency market."
Yushchenko said the bank would not place barriers on hard currency contracts for goods and services, but it would not allow speculative contracts.

The hryvnia slipped to 1.769 from 1.760 per dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange. It was the first time the hryvnia, which the central bank had been supporting on the exchange, had moved from 1.760 since it was introduced on September 2.
Yushchenko said speculative operations on the interbank market had increased and commercial banks were lax in applying rules with regard to deadlines and advance payments.
He said the hryvnia's slip was also due to imbalances in the budget and Ukraine's wage payment crisis, which now stands at $1.5 billion.

The central bank has tried to maintain the hryvnia at 1.76 to the dollar to prove the new currency was a success. It wanted to maintain calm among Ukrainians, who remembered the sharp devaluation of the temporary karbovanets currency when it was brought in.

Dealers said it was meeting up to 80 percent of demand for foreign currency on the exchange from its own reserves, spending $11-15 million a day instead of the $3-5 million a day it was spending before the hryvnia was introduced.

"The central bank decided to devalue the hryvnia by 0.9 kopeks, and although this is a bitter fact, everyone understands that the hryvnia does have the right to go up or down a little bit," said Yushchenko.
If the government backs central bank policy the hryvnia would soon return to its normal level, he added.
Any bank not obeying trading rules will face severe measures, Yushchenko said, including licence suspension. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
